claims.statement: convert-roms rewrites the library in place (new file next to the old one, old file deleted, romfiles row updated), while export-roms writes copies into a required -d/--directory and leaves both the originals and the database untouched, which is what makes lossy export targets safe.

ISO, GDI and WBFS exist only in export_roms' private format list, never in convert_roms::ALL_FORMATS; because config's PREFER_FORMAT choice list, the GraphQL PreferFormatValidator and the MCP tool all read ALL_FORMATS, those three can never become an auto-conversion target.

Tool availability gating treats every format as available except CHD, which probes the external chdman through util::tool_available; a failing probe prints 'Required tool not found: chdman' and is a soft stop returning Ok(()). export_roms repeats the same table inline but bails on an unknown format.

format_supported_for_system restricts arcade systems to ARCADE_FORMATS = [ORIGINAL, ZIP]; convert_system turns a violation into a warning and early return, and the same function is reused by config::set_setting, the GraphQL set_prefer_format mutation and the MCP tool so a rejected format cannot be stored through a validated surface.

ConvertOpts { recompress, diff, check, prompt_for_parents } is the shared entry to conversion: convert-roms builds it from -r/-d/-c/-p, and import_roms::auto_convert calls convert_system with recompress:false, diff:false, check:true, prompt_for_parents:false, catching errors as 'Auto-conversion to {format} failed' so a failed conversion never rolls back a completed import.

convert-roms --save writes the destination format straight into the per-system PREFER_FORMAT through set_string, bypassing the arcade validation the other writers apply; MCP's convert_roms tool instead reconstructs a convert-roms argv with only --system and --format, so MCP conversions never carry --recompress, --check or --save.
convert_system loads rom data with original_roms = true (only roms rows with original = true), while export_roms passes false and therefore also exports roms a DAT marks as non-original.

Compression settings are read per system (Some(system.id)) at conversion time: SEVENZIP_/ZIP_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM plus level keys and SEVENZIP_SOLID_COMPRESSION for archives, CHD_CD/DVD/HD/LD_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHMS, CHD_*_HUNK_SIZE and CHD_PARENTS for CHD, RVZ_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM/LEVEL/BLOCK_SIZE (plus RVZ_SCRUB only in export_roms) for RVZ; CSO, ZSO, NSZ and ORIGINAL read none.

The solid flag is threaded through ToArchive and read from SEVENZIP_SOLID_COMPRESSION (ZIP hard-codes false), but the archive writer ignores it because entries are added one call at a time, with a TODO to batch a game's files into one solid block.

Two chdman version gates skip work rather than failing: CHD conversion of a system whose name contains Dreamcast is skipped below MIN_DREAMCAST_VERSION (0.264), and every ChdType::Cd branch checks track_count > 1 against MIN_SPLITBIN_VERSION (0.265) before attempting to_cue_bin.

Every conversion decodes the source into a neutral artefact (ISO, CUE/BIN set, NSP) written into a fresh create_tmp_directory under TMP_DIRECTORY, wrapped with the originating romfile in transcode::Decoded { source, inner }, so the caller can diff and delete the source afterwards.

Each game (each CHD, each archive) is converted inside its own SQL transaction that is committed only on the success path; a skip or check failure leaves the transaction uncommitted so romfiles/roms rows revert, while any file already written has to be deleted explicitly by the branch.

check_and_persist is the generic commit tail: on a Check error it prints 'Integrity check failed, reverting conversion', deletes the new file and returns false; otherwise it optionally prints the diff, then updates the romfile row and deletes the source - or, with rename_to_source set (the recompression paths), deletes the source first and renames the new file onto the old path.

Integrity checking a converted CHD, XSO or archive means extracting it into a tmp directory and hashing the extracted bytes against the DAT's expected hash and size; RVZ hashes the disc in place instead. Failed conversion output is removed outright with remove_file, not moved to Trash.

Persist::update rewrites romfiles.path and romfiles.size for the same row id, so a converted file keeps its identity and every roms.romfile_id stays valid; only when a multi-file game collapses into one archive or one CHD does the code create or reuse a single row and re-point each rom with update_rom_romfile before deleting the old rows.

print_diff normalizes both sides against the DAT rather than the old file: Before and After are printed as percentages of the summed expected rom.size, so converting an already-compressed source still reports both relative to the uncompressed original.

to_archive partitions the loaded games by extension in a fixed order (CHD, CSO, NSZ, RVZ, ZSO, archive, then leftovers), sorts CHD games so children convert before parents, skips a CHD that still has children, and leaves arcade CHDs (any rom with rom.disk) untouched.

Archive-to-archive conversion is a no-op when the source archive type already matches the target unless --recompress is set; with recompress the archive is rebuilt into the tmp directory and renamed over the original path. The pair of tests asserts the distinction through the file's mtime.

Parent CHDs are chosen by find_parent_chd: prompt_for_parents (-p) lists the system's parentless CHDs sorted by jaro-winkler similarity to the game name, otherwise the CHD_PARENTS boolean falls back to find_parent_chd_romfile_by_game, which takes the first game of the game's playlist and that game's CHD romfile; the link is persisted with update_romfile_parent after each successful conversion.

CHD-to-CHD recompression only rewrites children: the parent CHD is skipped by the 'CHD has children, skipping' guard, and the test asserts the parent's mtime is unchanged while the child's moves forward.

CUE/BIN to CHD is the branch that leaves two romfiles behind: the generated .cue is renamed next to the source and kept as its own row, while every BIN rom is re-pointed at the new CHD row; more than one archive or one CHD inside a single game is a hard bail.

to_xso, to_nsz and to_rvz accept only narrow source sets and drop everything else: XSO takes single-ISO archives, loose ISOs, DVD CHDs and the opposite XSO type (always via a decoded ISO), NSZ takes NSPs and single-NSP archives, RVZ takes ISOs and single-ISO archives; same-format recompression happens in place only under --recompress, and convert_roms always passes scrub = false, never reading RVZ_SCRUB.
A multi-track CD CHD is deliberately left alone when converting to CSO/ZSO because transcode::chd_to_iso returns None for any CHD that is not a DVD, which is what the *_should_do_nothing tests pin.

convert_roms::to_original takes only the check flag (recompress and diff never reach it); for arcade systems an extracted archive expands into a new directory named after the archive stem, and if chdman disappears mid-run the CHD loop prints the missing-tool error and breaks instead of aborting the whole command.

export-roms opens no transaction and never calls Persist or Check: the destination directory is canonicalized and created up front, -o/--1g1r restricts the selection to games with sorting == Sorting::OneRegion, and every to_* function only writes files, so the database is read-only for the whole command.

export-roms copies rather than re-encodes sources that are already in the target format - ZIP to ZIP, 7z to 7z, CHD to CHD, CSO/ZSO either way, ISO to ISO and an existing GDI set with all its track files - with RVZ the exception: copied verbatim when RVZ_SCRUB is off, re-encoded through a temp ISO when it is on.

The export-only targets flatten rather than round-trip: to_iso keeps only the first track's 2048-byte user data (CD CHDs go CHD to CUE/BIN to ISO, HD/LD CHDs are skipped), to_wbfs writes a Wii WBFS from an ISO decoding RVZ through the tmp directory first, and to_gdi builds a GDI plus track files from CUE/BIN or copies an existing GDI set, skipping a CD CHD with no CUE alongside.

Conversion tests are one file per transition named test_<source>_to_<target>.rs and call the private to_* functions directly, passing recompress/diff/check and the CHD settings positionally; no-op transitions are asserted explicitly (*_should_do_nothing for convert, *_should_copy for export) and multi-track CHD tests return early when the installed chdman predates MIN_SPLITBIN_VERSION.
